title: StarterLabs sample-workbench handoff — smoke checks & quickstart gaps
body:
Purpose: capture the StarterLabs -> Samples Workbench handoff conversation, surface quickstart mismatches, and outline immediate smoke-test fixes for the public quickstart collection. This doc is chronicle + short-term action plan to avoid customer friction during the next onboarding wave.

Meeting snapshot (2026-06-24, 10:30–11:00 PST)
Attendees: Asha, Daniel, Sofia, Liam, Priya, 2 guests from Solutions Eng (Adrian, Mei).

Key context:
- We are shipping StarterLabs v2 (alpha) as a curated set of quickstarts and minimal apps that showcase Hosted API + Dedicated fallbacks. Samples repo is the canonical execution environment for those quickstarts.
- Recent smoke runs (local CI + cloud run) flagged failures in 4 quickstarts and slow cold-start times in Node quickstarts compared to Python counterparts.
- Observability gap: quickstart telemetry doesn't emit the "time-to-first-token" metric or sample-level cost estimate in README. New users are seeing 2–3x higher perceived latency.

Observed failures (short notes):
1) node-chat-quickstart: fails at npm run start with a thrown error from SDK v0.9.2 when streaming=true. Error: "Unhandled stream close: invalid chunk header". Repro steps in samples/recipes/node-chat/README.md.
2) embed-search-minimal: Python sample uses env var REDWOOD_MODEL alias that doesn't exist in hosted defaults; fallback prints an unhelpful traceback instead of a human message.
3) local-dedicated-demo: docker-compose memlock limits cause worker OOM in 8GB VMs (compose file uses default mem_increase helper).
4) reranker-example: sample assumes reranking endpoint returns 'scores' field; new hosted response returns 'ranking' — mismatch from swagger update last week.

Metric readouts from smoke runs (comparing node vs python):
- node-chat-quickstart cold TTF token: median 420ms, p95 1.8s (local vm x86, no GPU)
- python-chat-quickstart cold TTF token: median 160ms, p95 360ms
- sample test pass rate (latest run): 87% overall, quickstarts folder only 73% (target >= 95%)

Root-cause hypotheses:
- SDK Node stream implementation has a fragile backpressure handling edge with our streaming protocol version bump in June.
- Quickstarts docs drift with API changes (env var names, response shapes); no automation currently validates README examples against live responses.
- Docker/local defaults tuned for internal infra; external users on small VMs hit resource assumptions.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Fast path: patch the node streaming client to gracefully handle the invalid-chunk error and fall back to chunked-buffer model; ship a patch release 0.9.3-canary. Owner: Daniel. Target: 2026-06-29.
- Docs path: add a small "sanity-check" CI job that runs each quickstart with a smoke harness and validates three things: exits 0, returns expected JSON schema (lightweight), and reports TTF <= 1s for sample seeds. Owner: Sofia. Target PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/256 (in progress).
- Env var mapping: create a compatibility shim for REDWOOD_MODEL -> REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL in the Python quickstarts and add deprecation note. Owner: Priya. Target: 2026-06-26.
- Docker resources: add a reduced-memory profile (docker-compose-lite.yml) and a health-check that suggests increasing ulimit/memlock if OOM occurs. Owner: Liam. Target: 2026-07-02.
- API contract: add a conformance test that checks response fields (scores vs ranking) against a small matrix of models we support. This will be part of the samples CI; owner: Solutions Eng (Adrian). Target: 2026-07-05.

Action items (tangible list)
- Daniel Park: open SDK canary release with node-stream fallback and add test that reproduces invalid chunk header (due 2026-06-29).
- Sofia Gutierrez: implement samples/smoke CI job, wire to GitHub Actions, add minimal schema checks and timeouts (due 2026-06-28).
- Priya Sharma: patch Python quickstarts for env var compatibility + plain-language error messages; add tiny troubleshooting section to README (due 2026-06-26).
- Liam O'Connor: add docker-compose-lite.yml, update README with local resource guidance and a link to the SRE memlock doc (due 2026-07-02).
- Adrian (Solutions Eng): design conformance matrix for response shapes and own the small test harness (due 2026-07-05).
- Asha Mehta: coordinate StarterLabs alpha launch checklist (include analytics events, docs links, and quickstart smoke pass). Kick-off to engineering + comms (due 2026-06-30).

Short-term FAQs to include in README updates:
- Q: Why does node chat feel slower?
  A: Node SDK stream uses a different buffering path; can be fixed via 0.9.3 patch. Workaround: set streaming=false for quickstart demos until patched.
- Q: What memory should I allocate for the local Dedicated demo?
  A: 16GB recommended for a multi-worker demo. For single dev machine, use docker-compose-lite and bind to a single worker.

Follow-ups and risks:
- Risk: If SDK patch slips, marketing alpha launch will show failing quickstarts; contingency: feature-flag the StarterLabs launch page to hide live-run buttons and show walkthrough-only steps. Marketing/Comms coordination needed.
- Follow-up sync: 2026-06-29, 09:00 PST, 15m standup to check on Daniel/Sofia progress and unblock PR reviews.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas (brain dump):
- Consider adding a tiny telemetry beacon in quickstarts that reports anonymized boot metrics (TTF, token counts) to a central sandbox metrics bucket for future baseline comparisons. Privacy checklist required.
- Add a "verify-readme" npm/pip dev tool that runs examples and fails CI if output drifts. Could be part of SDK dev tooling.
- Long-term: include per-quickstart cost-estimate badges (tokens/min, infra cost estimate) for transparency.

Appendix (debug snippets)
- Repro command for node-chat error: cd samples/recipes/node-chat && NODE_ENV=dev REDWOOD_API_KEY=__red__ npm ci && npm run smoke -- --seed=short-convo
- Minimal python compatibility check snippet: python -c "import os, sys; m=os.getenv('REDWOOD_MODEL') or os.getenv('REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL'); print('model=',m);"
action_items: Daniel: SDK node streaming fallback + canary release (due 2026-06-29)
Sofia: samples smoke CI job + schema checks (due 2026-06-28)
Priya: env var shim + README troubleshooting (due 2026-06-26)
Asha: StarterLabs alpha launch checklist + comms sync (due 2026-06-30)
